newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador accuses top businessman of fraud.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador accuses top businessman of fraud.

text.p: Authorities on Wednesday said they arrested several executives of a private bank and that they were seeking its owner, one of El Salvador's top businessmen, on fraud charges.

In a statement issued late on Wednesday, the country's highest tax authority said it was seeking the detention of Roberto Mathies Hill, a high-profile businessman closely tied to the ruling party, for "defrauding the public."
Mathies Hill is owner of Finsepro, a financial firm that is accused of bilking local investors of tens of millions of dollars.

Mathies Hill's plush house in San Salvador was surrounded by rapid-response police units and anti-drug inspectors. A police helicopter flew overhead and agents stood atop ladders propped against its high perimeter wall.
"There is nothing official," said Elena Miranda, spokeswoman for the Superintendency for Financial Institutions. "But I can't say it's not happening because everyone knows it is."
Mathies Hill is a member of a business group directly linked to the ruling Nationalist Republican Alliance (ARENA). He is also head of the country's football selection committee.

Scores of furious investors lined up at Finsepro on Wednesday after local media circulated reports of the fraud. According to the reports, the accused are charged with embezzling at least $30 million from investment accounts at Finsepro.

"We came to take out our investments, they said they would give them to us, but they haven't given us anything," a young Salvadorean lawyer told reporters outside the headquarters of Finsepro in the capital.
